newsitem.title: USA: CalPERS unveils governance proposal for U.S. cos.
newsitem.headline: CalPERS unveils governance proposal for U.S. cos.

text.p: California's Public Employees' Retirement System -- the nation's largest public pension fund -- unveiled Monday a set of proposed governance guidelines for U.S. companies in its $113 billion portfolio.

The proposed "corporate governance" principles for the U.S. market were designed to boost the independence and accountability of company boards, and the value of the system's domestic stock holdings, CalPERS staff said.
The CalPERS investment committee was expected to vote on the staff proposal at Monday's meeting in Sacramento, but instead deferred action to study the guidelines further.
The committee may vote on the plan at its scheduled meeting in August, a spokesman for the pension system said.
Under the proposed principles for U.S. companies:

* A majority of a company's board would consist of directors who are independent. No director would be considered independent after having served 10 or more years on the company's board. Ideally, no more than 10 percent of the directors would be over the age of 70.
* When the chair of a company's board also serves as the company's chief executive officer, the board should designate an independent director who acts in a lead capacity.
* Company directors would be compensated with a combination of cash and stock. Ideally, CalPERS said at least 50 percent of a director's total compensation would be stock.

* A company's board would adopt a written statement of its own governance principles and re-evaluate them every two to three years. The board would also set performance criteria for itself and individual goals for its directors.

If approved by CalPERS later this year, the pension fund would ask the top 300 companies in its U.S. portfolio to address these principles. CalPERS would then issue a report that would evaluate their efforts.
Companies that fail to comply with the proposed standards could face corporate governance fights and board shakeups, CalPERS staff said.
In March, CalPERS adopted similar corporate governance principles for France and Germany.
CalPERS is the largest public pension fund in the United States and the third largest in the world, with assets totaling more than $113 billion.
The fund provides retirement and health benefits to more than one million public employees and their families.
